context: Interactive sunburst chart (Product Taxonomy Explorer) with 4-level product hierarchy (root → departments → categories → products), radial brush for outer-ring selection, click-to-zoom, breadcrumb trail, and sidebar stats showing selected count and revenue.
first_impression: Structurally honest sunburst using d3.partition() with data-driven angular area encoding, though synthetic data and missing key functions cap the ceiling.
what_works: Angular area faithfully encodes revenue via root.sum() and d3.partition() — proportions are mathematically correct; color encodes only categorical department identity (not quantitative data), avoiding false magnitude encoding.
what_doesnt: No key functions (.data(descendants, d => d.id)) in the path join — harmless given the single-build pattern but breaks object constancy if data were re-joined; depth-adjusted lightness/chroma within each hue subtly implies a second data dimension that doesn't exist, risking misreading depth as a quantitative signal.
